title: Test: lessons 11–18
description: Forms, CSS variables, JavaScript: variables, conditions, loops, functions, arrays, objects. 15 minutes. No points: −100 XP per mistake, leaving the test −2000 XP.

questions.prompt: A click on the word «Email». What happens?
options: Nothing — for and id don't match
The browser shows an error in the console
The field highlights but the cursor doesn't go in
The cursor goes into the field
questions.explain: A label links to a field only if for equals id. Here email ≠ mail, so there's no link.
nth-child counts all siblings, including h3. h3 is 1st, the paragraphs are in places 2–5. Odd places are 3 and 5 — paragraphs «2» and «4».
p:first-child is a paragraph that is the parent's first child. Here the first child is h2, so the rule applies to nothing.

questions.prompt: What color will the heading be? (It comes after the card, not inside it.)
questions.explain: A variable declared in .card is visible only inside the card. Global variables are declared in :root.

questions.prompt: How will the button background change?
options: Smoothly only when the cursor leaves
Smoothly on hover and abruptly when the cursor leaves
questions.explain: transition is only in :hover. When the cursor leaves, the :hover rule stops working along with the transition. It belongs in the main .btn rule.

questions.prompt: How many times will the button «breathe»?
questions.explain: By default an animation plays once. To repeat it you need infinite.
+ with a string glues: "51". - doesn't work with strings, so JS turns the string into a number: 4.

options: Error — const can't be reassigned, console.log won't run
questions.explain: TypeError: Assignment to constant variable. After the error the code stops.
"18" is a string, 18 is a number. === also compares types, so it's false. This happens with input field values — they're always strings.
Conditions are checked top to bottom. 95 ≥ 70 — the first is already true, the rest are skipped. Check bigger thresholds first.
a > 3 is true, but a < 5 is false (5 isn't less than 5). && needs both to be true.
i goes from 1 to 9. The remainder of dividing by 3 is zero for 3, 6 and 9.

options: An infinite loop: 0 is printed endlessly
questions.explain: i++ is after the loop, not inside. i is always 0, the condition is always true — the browser freezes.
There's no return — the function computes but gives nothing back.
No argument was passed — the name parameter is undefined and it gets glued to the string.
fruits.length is 3, but the last index is 2. There's no element at index 3. The last one: fruits[fruits.length - 1].
forEach returns nothing. map returns a new array.
filter keeps [12, 20] (8 isn't greater than 8), length is 2.

questions.code:
const { name, age } = { name: "Anya" };
console.log(name, age);
questions.explain: The object has no age field — the age variable gets undefined, no error.
user.key looks for a field called key — there isn't one. user[key] uses the variable's value — it looks for name.
